name: opencode
one_liner: A free, open-source AI coding assistant you install yourself, similar in spirit to Claude Code, that you can run in a terminal or desktop app.
buyer: A developer or small team who wants an AI coding assistant without being locked into one vendor's model or pricing, and is comfortable self-hosting and configuring it.
business_use_cases: A dev agency standardizes on it so clients aren't billed for a specific vendor's subscription, and the agency can swap in whichever model is cheapest that month.
A platform team builds and sells custom agents or plugins on top of it for a specific tech stack (e.g. a Rails or Django specialist agent).
A privacy-sensitive company runs it against a locally-hosted model to keep code entirely off third-party servers.

money_ideas.idea: Build and sell a specialized agent or plugin for it targeting one niche tech stack or workflow that the generic defaults don't handle well.

steal_this: Set it up against a cheap open-weight model this weekend and compare its output quality and cost against whatever paid tool you currently use.
